Both are strong, but I still lean toward B—"What Will You Discover?" directly invites students in and sparks curiosity. That said, A is genuinely clever and memorable, so if you prefer it, that's a very defensible choice!

A

Option A creates an ongoing, escalating problem that plays out live during the performance itself—the actor delivering last year's lines mid-scene while everyone scrambles is a richer engine for character-driven comedy. Option B is a funny visual gag, but it tends to be a logistical hiccup that gets resolved, whereas A keeps generating fresh conflict. That said, B is a perfectly good choice if you want more absurd, visual humor—your instinct isn't wrong. What's the tone you're going for?

A

I'll stick with A. The wrong-props gag is funny but tends to be a one-note visual joke. A lead actor confidently delivering *last year's* lines is a recurring, character-driven problem—it forces everyone else to react and adapt in real time, escalates naturally, and pays off emotionally. That said, B could work well as a secondary running gag alongside it.
